definitions.explanation: The act of pressing someone to do something quickly or fulfill an obligation.

examples.japanese: {支払|しはら}いの{催促|さいそく}が{来|き}た。
{上司|じょうし}に{報告書|ほうこくしょ}の{催促|さいそく}をされた。
examples.english: I was pressed by my boss for the report.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}も{催促|さいそく}しても{返事|へんじ}がない。
examples.english: Even after repeated reminders, there is no reply.

notes:
{催促|さいそく} means urging or pressing someone to do something they should have already done—often regarding payments, responses, or deadlines.

GRAMMAR:
- Functions as noun or する verb: {催促|さいそく}する (to urge, to press)
- Often used in passive: {催促|さいそく}される (to be pressed/reminded)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {催促|さいそく}を{受|う}ける (to receive a reminder)
- {催促|さいそく}{状|じょう} (reminder letter, dunning letter)
- {支払|しはら}いの{催促|さいそく} (payment reminder)
- {何度|なんど}も{催促|さいそく}する (to remind repeatedly)

NUANCE:
Implies some frustration or urgency—the person being urged is behind schedule or has not responded. More direct than {お願|ねが}いする.

RELATED WORDS:
- {督促|とくそく}: stronger/more formal demand (often legal)
- {請求|せいきゅう}: billing, invoice request
